result: Exact rmcp-v3.1.4 Streamable HTTP source shows the legacy/sessionful POST path also injects consumed http::request::Parts into the MCP request/notification Extensions before session dispatch. The existing-session branch validates protocol and standard headers, then inserts part into request or notification extensions; the legacy initialize/session-creation branch likewise inserts part into the initialize request before the spawned session worker serves it. Combined with the already-proven generic serve loop that moves request Extensions into RequestContext.extensions while RequestMetaObject remains RequestContext.meta, trusted server-side HTTP middleware state remains reachable through RequestContext.extensions -> http::request::Parts -> Parts.extensions on these legacy/sessionful POST paths, without using client _meta as identity authority.
trusted_principal_contract: For exact rmcp-v3.1.4 normal Streamable HTTP POST handling in both stateless and legacy/sessionful branches, authenticate in trusted HTTP middleware, store Principal in the inbound HTTP request extensions, then in the tool handler read RequestContext.extensions::<http::request::Parts>() and Parts.extensions::<Principal>(); fail closed if either is absent. Do not accept RequestMetaObject/client _meta as principal authority. Cross-instance restore/replayed initialize semantics remain unverified and are excluded from this claim.
